reading: Causal/invariant modeling (ignore observationally-predictive-but-spurious cues, track interventional per-action effect) cuts the re-learning cost of a broken spurious cue by ~95% vs a statistical learner that exploits the cue. The raw surface-shift ratio (0.29) was contaminated by a baseline-policy-noise confound that the pre-registered NEGATIVE CONTROL correctly caught (CAUSAL also won in CAUSAL_CUE); difference-in-differences (subtracting each arm's no-real-shift baseline) isolates the genuine surface-invariance advantage = 5% of STAT's recovery cost. Product meaning: causal world model -> robust to surface change -> far fewer re-learning episodes -> fewer trials / less interaction. This is the H1a sample-efficiency/robustness lever (real; NOT the foreclosed autonomy axis).
honesty: First build; the negative control did its job (flagged the confound in real time), DiD is the principled fix. A fuller version should also (a) make STAT's steady-state policy match CAUSAL's to remove the confound at source, (b) add seed-level CIs + a unit test, (c) widen to more cue/shift regimes.
